Deciding between paying the $50 jail fine or rolling for doubles.

Analyzing opponent holdings to assess risk. p2 has incomplete orange, red, and yellow sets. p3 owns a brown monopoly with hotels. Evaluating whether the $50 fine is worth paying to land on Virginia Ave first.

p4 owns a jail card and is in good financial shape. Virginia Ave is bank-owned at $160, which would complete the pink set. The remaining unowned properties are Virginia, Tennessee, Kentucky, Illinois, B&O, Atlantic, Pacific, and North Carolina.

Tennessee is still bank-owned. I will not sell Vermont to p4. Staying liquid is the priority for Virginia and Tennessee. I have already served one turn in jail.

Turn 47 was a 6+2 roll where I paid the $50 fine and left jail. I am now back in jail at turn 51 after serving one turn without rolling doubles.

I need to leave jail immediately. I cannot afford to stay in it while p2 and p4 are actively buying properties. I must land on Virginia Ave before others claim it.

Paying the $50 fine leaves $1,163. That covers Virginia Ave and Tennessee Ave plus building houses on the pink set. Rolling doubles is only a 1 in 6 chance. If I fail, I would serve another turn in jail while opponents move freely around the board.
